Both adapters start at 0 with separate, fully reserved specialists, so their joint finish time is max(A, B). Coding, tests and review are already included in their durations. The additional combined acceptance day follows both finishes:

- Both take 2 days: probability 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64. Adapters finish at 2, combined acceptance finishes at 3, and deployment acceptance occurs at slot 4.
- At least one takes 6 days: probability 1 − 0.64 = 0.36. Adapters finish at 6, combined acceptance finishes at 7, and deployment acceptance occurs at slot 8.

Thus cumulative completion probability is 64% at time 4 and 100% at time 8. Time 8 is the earliest completion time reaching at least 80%; discrete outcomes make its coverage exceed 80%. Individual task P80s of 2 days do not establish the project percentile: only 64% of outcomes have both adapters finished by time 2.

I recommend retaining time 8 as the planning target. The forecast supports it under the supplied assumptions, but elicited inputs have no historical calibration, and a forecast does not itself create a promise. No commitment has been made.
